assets.content:
PRESS PDF — Thornmere Home spring catalogue (24 pages, one product to a page, A5 portrait 148 x 210 mm, 3mm bleed, fonts embedded). What the printer still has on file; the old studio kept the working InDesign. To be reverse-engineered into a live merge template and rebuilt for autumn as 32 pages.

PER-PAGE VISUAL STRUCTURE (top to bottom):
1. PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPH — a large placed image, upper ~60% of the page, on the warm paper ground.
2. CAPTION STACK — what reads on the printed page as a stack of separate lines but converts into a single continuous text flow:
   PRODUCT NAME (humanist serif, e.g. 'Oatmeal Breakfast Mug')
   DIMENSIONS line (quiet grotesque, e.g. 'H 95 x Dia 85 mm')
   MATERIALS line (e.g. 'Glazed stoneware')
   CARE line (the maker's own words, e.g. 'Dishwasher safe.') -- this is the run the converted-story readout drops while keeping its line break
   PRICE (e.g. '$45')

MERGE FIELD LABELS (to be mapped from thornmere_autumn_skus.csv, by offset within the single caption story):
<<product_name>>  ->  PRODUCT NAME
<<dimensions>>  ->  DIMENSIONS line
<<materials>>  ->  MATERIALS line
<<care_line>>  ->  CARE line (do not reword the maker's wording)
<<price>>  ->  PRICE line
<<picture_filename>>  ->  PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPH (bound through the @-prefixed image column)

NOTE FOR THE PRINTER: warm paper ground #F6F1E8, near-black text, generous leading and air, nothing cut off at trim, the care line matters as much as the price. Page trim 148 x 210 mm. Spring run was 24 products; autumn run is 32.

assets.defect_engineered: 32 records for the one-product-per-page merge (24-page spring template rebuilt to 32); care_line ranges from three words to two full sentences (the long ones overrun a fixed caption frame and stop rendering); THREE SKUs (TH-008, TH-014, TH-019) point at styled-pair frames (autumn_shoot_10 / _04 / _07) so those three products have NO solo photograph and nothing in the sheet says so; picture_filename references the 20 supplied frames with realistic reuse; care lines are the maker's own words (do not reword)
